$comment: Exceptions to the license allowlist (tools/licensing/policy.json). Each must reference an ADR. status: accepted = owner-approved; pending-owner = allowed in CI with a warning until the owner accepts or rejects it in the referenced ADR. Matching is by ecosystem + name + license + scope, so a license change upstream re-opens the question.

exceptions.name: mediabunny
exceptions.reason: Optional transitive dependency of werift (S1's WebRTC DataChannel experiment); used unmodified from npm and not bundled into any web page. MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: obligations apply only to modified MPL files, which we don't have.
exceptions.revisit: Before any product build that ships werift; prefer a WebRTC path without it, or accept MPL-2.0 for unmodified npm dependencies in a superseding ADR.

exceptions.name: tweetnacl
exceptions.reason: Optional transitive dependency of werift and @fidm/x509 (S1). The Unlicense is an OSI-approved public-domain dedication with a permissive fallback; no attribution or copyleft obligations.
exceptions.revisit: Recommend adding Unlicense to the allowlist in ADR-0008.

exceptions.name: YARC-Official/YARG.Core
exceptions.reason: S2/S3 spike harnesses fetch YARG.Core at a pinned commit (S2) or as the fork's submodule (S3) into gitignored external/ folders and build against it. Nothing is vendored; the harness source stays MIT.
exceptions.revisit: Never vendor. Any product use needs its own ADR (ADR-0004 already rules out a product dependency on YARG).

exceptions.name: dcuccia/YARG (branch handbell-spike)
exceptions.reason: The YARG fork (community track, ADR-0004) is fetched by S3's harness and by tools/setup/setup-yarg.ps1; it lives in its own LGPL repository.
exceptions.revisit: Author fork code here first (MIT) and contribute it outbound, per ADR-0008.

exceptions.name: spikes/s2-yarg-core/patches/0001-yarglogger-no-thread-on-browser.diff
exceptions.reason: A unified diff against YARG.Core's YargLogger.cs. Its context lines are YARG.Core code, so the file is labeled LGPL-3.0-or-later (REUSE.toml) rather than MIT. fetch-yarg-core.ps1 applies the same change without the diff.
exceptions.revisit: Owner: keep it as a clearly labeled LGPL file, or delete it (the fetch script reproduces the patch) and keep the draft upstream issue in the S2 report.
